items.q: Mai ______ three novels by that author since January.
items.vi: Từ tháng Một đến giờ Mai đã đọc ba cuốn tiểu thuyết của tác giả đó.
items.explanation: Since January marks a period running from a past starting point up to now, so the present perfect has read is required. ✗ read — past simple describes a finished time, but the period is still open; ✗ is reading — present continuous is for an action happening right now, not a total of three finished books; ✗ had read — past perfect needs a later past event to be earlier than, and there is none.

items.q: My sister ______ the ending of the film in my ear so that nobody else in the cinema could hear.
items.vi: Chị tôi thì thầm vào tai tôi đoạn kết của bộ phim để không ai khác trong rạp nghe thấy.
items.explanation: So that nobody else could hear means the words were said very quietly, and in my ear confirms it: whispered = spoke very softly. ✗ shouted — spoke very loudly, the opposite; ✗ announced — told everyone publicly; ✗ declared — stated openly and firmly, not secretly.

items.q: We ______ a lot of money on new furniture for the living room.
items.vi: Chúng tôi đã tiêu rất nhiều tiền vào đồ nội thất mới cho phòng khách.
items.explanation: Money is the object and on new furniture names what it was used for, so the collocation is spend money on something. ✗ paid — you pay a person or pay for a thing, never pay money on it; ✗ cost — the thing costs money (the furniture cost us a lot), the buyer does not; ✗ took — take money = pick it up or accept it, not use it to buy.

items.q: Relax – it is only a tiny scratch on the car door. Don't ______.
options: put all your eggs in one basket
bite off more than you can chew
kill two birds with one stone
make a mountain out of a molehill
items.answer: make a mountain out of a molehill
items.vi: Bình tĩnh đi, chỉ là một vết xước nhỏ xíu trên cửa xe thôi. Đừng có chuyện bé xé ra to.
items.explanation: Only a tiny scratch plus relax means a small problem is being treated as a huge one: make a mountain out of a molehill = exaggerate a small problem. ✗ put all your eggs in one basket — risk everything on one plan; ✗ bite off more than you can chew — take on more than you can manage; ✗ kill two birds with one stone — achieve two things with one action.

items.q: We waited an hour outside the cinema, but Nam never ______.
items.vi: Chúng tôi đợi cả tiếng ngoài rạp chiếu phim, nhưng Nam chẳng bao giờ xuất hiện.
items.explanation: Waited an hour ... but never means Nam did not arrive: turned up = appeared, arrived. ✗ put up — needs an object (put up a poster) or with (put up with = tolerate); ✗ turned down — refused, or lowered the volume; ✗ turned off — switched off a device.

items.q: Nam ______ at the concert last night – I saw him at home at nine o'clock.
items.vi: Tối qua Nam không thể nào ở buổi hòa nhạc được – lúc chín giờ tôi thấy cậu ấy ở nhà mà.
items.explanation: I saw him at home at nine is proof that his being at the concert was impossible, so the negative past deduction can't have been is needed. ✗ mustn't have been — must have is only for positive deduction; its negative is can't have; ✗ needn't have been — it was not necessary, but he did it anyway; ✗ shouldn't have been — it was wrong of him to be there, a criticism, not a conclusion about facts.

items.q: The coach with ______ we trained for the swimming competition has moved to another club.
items.vi: Huấn luyện viên mà chúng tôi đã tập luyện cùng cho giải bơi đã chuyển sang câu lạc bộ khác.
items.explanation: The pronoun directly follows the preposition with and refers to a person (the coach), so the object form whom is required: with whom we trained. ✗ who — subject form, not used straight after a preposition; ✗ whose — possessive, must be followed by a noun; ✗ which — for things, not people.

items.q: Linh has visited ______ countries in Asia, but she has never been to Japan.
items.vi: Linh đã đi thăm vài nước ở châu Á, nhưng cô ấy chưa từng đến Nhật Bản.
items.explanation: Countries is plural countable, and but never Japan shows some, not all, were visited, so several (= a few, more than two) fits. ✗ much — only with uncountable nouns (much money); ✗ a little — only with uncountable nouns (a little time); ✗ every — takes a singular noun (every country) and would contradict never having been to Japan.

items.q: Could you ______ the last scene to me? I didn't understand why the hero left.
items.vi: Bạn giải thích cảnh cuối cho mình được không? Mình không hiểu tại sao nhân vật chính lại bỏ đi.
items.explanation: I didn't understand shows the speaker wants the scene made clear: explain something to someone = make it clear. ✗ complain — say you are unhappy (complain about something), not clarify; ✗ persuade — make a person agree to do something, so its object is a person, not a scene; ✗ argue — disagree in words (argue with someone), not make something clear.

items.q: Remember ______ the front door when you go out this evening.
items.vi: Nhớ khóa cửa trước khi con ra ngoài tối nay nhé.
items.explanation: When you go out this evening puts the locking in the future, so it is a task still to do: remember to do = don't forget to do it. ✗ locking — remember doing = recall something already done, a memory not an instruction; ✗ lock — remember is never followed by a bare infinitive; ✗ to locking — to + -ing is not a form remember takes.

items.q: Nam still went to school ______ he had a bad cold and a sore throat.
items.vi: Nam vẫn đi học mặc dù cậu ấy bị cảm nặng và đau họng.
items.explanation: The blank is followed by a full clause with subject and verb (he had), so the contrast word must be a conjunction: although. ✗ despite — preposition, followed by a noun or -ing (despite his cold), not a clause; ✗ in spite of — same, needs a noun or -ing; ✗ however — adverb that starts a new sentence (However, he ...), it cannot join two clauses inside one sentence.

items.q: Could you ______ me to call Grandma tonight? I always forget.
items.vi: Bạn nhắc mình gọi cho bà tối nay nhé? Mình lúc nào cũng quên.
items.explanation: I always forget means the speaker needs someone to make them remember, and the pattern is remind someone to do something. ✗ suggest — takes suggest doing / suggest that, never suggest someone to do; ✗ recommend — takes recommend doing / recommend that, not recommend someone to do; ✗ mention — speak briefly about something; mention someone to do does not exist.

items.q: I wish I ______ the film last night – everyone at school is talking about it.
items.vi: Giá mà tối qua tôi đã xem bộ phim đó – ở trường ai cũng đang bàn về nó.
items.explanation: Last night makes this a wish about the past, and past wishes take wish + past perfect: had seen. ✗ saw — past simple after wish is a wish about the present (I wish I saw him more often); ✗ have seen — present perfect is never used after wish; ✗ would see — wish + would is for wanting a future change or complaining about someone's behaviour.

items.q: Could you ______ me a favour and return this book to the library?
items.vi: Bạn giúp mình một việc, trả cuốn sách này về thư viện được không?
items.explanation: Favour as a small act of help has one fixed verb: do someone a favour. ✗ make — make goes with a decision, a mistake, an effort, not a favour; ✗ give — you give help or advice, but not give a favour; ✗ take — take does not combine with favour at all.

items.q: The film ______ in Da Lat last year, which is why the scenery looks so familiar.
items.vi: Bộ phim được quay ở Đà Lạt năm ngoái, vì thế cảnh trong phim trông rất quen thuộc.
items.explanation: A film is shot by people, so the verb must be passive, and last year fixes the past simple: was shot. ✗ shot — active past, meaning the film did the shooting; ✗ has shot — active, and present perfect cannot be used with a finished time like last year; ✗ is shot — passive but present, contradicting last year.

items.q: This time next week, my family ______ in our new house on the other side of town.
items.vi: Vào giờ này tuần sau, gia đình tôi sẽ đang sống trong ngôi nhà mới ở phía bên kia thành phố.
items.explanation: This time next week names an exact future moment, and an action that will be in progress at that moment takes the future continuous: will be living. ✗ live — present simple states a general fact, no future meaning here; ✗ will live — plain future prediction, does not show an action in progress at a point in time; ✗ are living — present continuous describes now, not next week.

items.q: Mum asked me where ______ the TV remote after the film.
items.vi: Mẹ hỏi tôi đã để cái điều khiển ti vi ở đâu sau khi xem phim.
items.explanation: Asked me where introduces a reported question, which keeps statement order subject + verb and shifts the past simple back one step after past asked: where I had put. ✗ had I put — inverted verb-subject order belongs only to direct questions; ✗ did I put — the question auxiliary did is dropped in reported questions; ✗ have I put — inverted, and present perfect is not the backshifted form of past simple.

items.q: After a long talk, my parents and I are finally ______ about my plan to study music.
items.vi: Sau một cuộc nói chuyện dài, cuối cùng bố mẹ và tôi cũng đã đồng quan điểm về kế hoạch học nhạc của tôi.
items.explanation: After a long talk ... finally means they now agree about the plan: on the same page = sharing the same understanding. ✗ in the same boat — in the same difficult situation; ✗ under the weather — slightly ill; ✗ over the moon — extremely happy.

items.q: My sister is really keen ______ Korean pop music and knows every song by heart.
items.vi: Chị tôi rất mê nhạc pop Hàn Quốc và thuộc lòng mọi bài hát.
items.explanation: Keen meaning very interested takes the fixed preposition on: keen on Korean pop music. ✗ in — goes with interested (interested in), not keen; ✗ of — goes with fond (fond of), not keen; ✗ at — goes with good / bad (good at), not keen.

items.q: Please don't ______ while Grandma is telling her story – wait until she finishes.
items.vi: Đừng ngắt lời khi bà đang kể chuyện – hãy đợi bà kể xong đã.
items.explanation: While Grandma is telling her story – wait until she finishes tells you the problem is speaking before she has finished: interrupt = break in while someone is talking. ✗ repeat — say again, and it needs an object (repeat the story); ✗ describe — say what something is like, needs an object; ✗ pronounce — say the sounds of a word, needs an object and has nothing to do with waiting.

items.q: My parents couldn't ______ how to use the new TV remote, so I showed them.
items.vi: Bố mẹ tôi không tìm ra cách dùng cái điều khiển ti vi mới, nên tôi chỉ cho họ.
items.explanation: Couldn't ... how to use and so I showed them mean they failed to find the answer: work out = understand or solve by thinking. ✗ work up — build up an appetite, courage or energy; ✗ carry out — perform or complete a task or order; ✗ set out — start a journey, or lay out plans.

items.q: The more pocket money you save now, ______ you can spend on the school trip.
items.vi: Bây giờ bạn càng để dành nhiều tiền tiêu vặt, thì bạn càng có nhiều tiền để chi cho chuyến đi của trường.
items.explanation: The sentence opens with The more ... you save, and the double comparative pattern needs the + comparative in both halves: the more. ✗ more — comparative but missing the required the; ✗ the most — superlative, not a comparative; ✗ most — superlative and without the.

items.q: By the time the film ended, the painkiller ______, and my tooth hurt again.
items.vi: Đến lúc bộ phim kết thúc thì thuốc giảm đau đã hết tác dụng, và răng tôi lại đau.
items.explanation: By the time the film ended (past simple) fixes a past moment, and the painkiller stopped working before it, so the earlier action takes the past perfect: had worn off (= stopped having an effect). ✗ wore off — past simple would make the two events happen together, not one before the other; ✗ has worn off — present perfect cannot follow a past-time clause; ✗ wears off — present simple, but the story is in the past.

items.q: The bookshop ______ a twenty per cent discount on all novels this week.
items.vi: Tuần này hiệu sách giảm giá hai mươi phần trăm cho tất cả tiểu thuyết.
items.explanation: The subject is a shop and the object is a ... discount; the collocation is offer (or give) a discount. ✗ makes — make goes with a profit or a purchase, not a discount; ✗ does — do a deal exists, but do a discount is not English; ✗ brings — bring = carry something to a place, it does not go with discount.

items.q: The shop assistant ______ that the phone was cheaper online, so we didn't buy it there.
items.vi: Nhân viên cửa hàng thừa nhận rằng chiếc điện thoại mua trên mạng rẻ hơn, nên chúng tôi không mua ở đó.
items.explanation: So we didn't buy it there shows the assistant agreed to an unwelcome truth about his own shop: admitted that = confessed something was true. ✗ denied — said it was not true, which would not make the buyers leave; ✗ refused — takes to + verb, not a that-clause; ✗ promised that — a promise makes no sense with a cheaper price elsewhere and would not lead to not buying.
